title: Extra Point Previews: Geneva Panthers seek turnaround in Year Three under Harris after winless 2024 - NewsBreak
text: GENEVA, Ala (WDHN) — Entering his third season at the helm, head coach Jamel Harris faces the challenge of rebuilding a Geneva program that went winless in 2024 and has won just three games over the past two years. The Panthers, who scored 11.3 points per game and allowed 32.1 last fall, return a veteran core but will again rely on two-way players to compete in Class 4A, Region 2. Geneva brings back eight starters on offense, led by senior running back and safety J.J. King, a versatile athlete who will see time in multiple roles. Sophomore Tucker Taylor takes over at quarterback after starting as a freshman at tight end and playing various positions on defense. Senior wideout Hayden Love, junior receiver Braylon Sims, and senior linemen Dawson Smith and Judd Derouen add experience to the unit. The Panthers also return nine defensive starters, including a deep front anchored by sophomores Gracin Beagles, Hunter Shiver, and C.J. Scott, along with junior Carter Spears. Linebackers Samuel Cade and Jeffrey Woods lead the middle, while Soles, Landon Mixon, and King anchor the secondary. Harris isn’t dwelling on the past. “No where to go, but up,” he said. “Last year we put that in the past… nothing we can do about it except harp on it and it ain’t going to change anything. So we keep moving forward one day at a time, try to get better one day at a time.” He believes the formula is simple: “Effort, attitude and toughness — if we bring those three things, we have a chance. We don’t have as many players anymore… we’re down to the ones that really want to play football and really want to buy in. I think we’re getting tougher. We’ve been working hard in the weight room and the hot sun. You don’t have to be really big to be a high school football player — just do things the right way, have a great attitude and be tough.” Replacing a talent like Dalton Mock will be by committee. “We’ve had a few kids come out that are just as athletic as he was and they’re buying in,” Harris said. “One player doesn’t make us anymore. We have other guys getting touches many different ways — we’re going to do it together, collectively.” Harris says last season’s record didn’t tell the whole story. “We lost a game by two points right at the end, and about three games with 10 seconds to go. We have to find a way to finish those games this year. With this bunch, I believe we’ll be able to finish more for sure.” King headlines a group of players Harris trusts. “He’ll be a four-year starter… linebacker, safety, running back, a little quarterback,” Harris said. “Last year he had a little slump, but he’s back to the form he was when he was younger.” He’s also intrigued by sophomore C.J. Scott, senior newcomer Zerek Hall, and linebacker Samuel Cade, who was lost to a knee injury in Week 2 last year. “I’m taking over calling defenses… I’m focusing a lot more on our linebackers,” Harris said. “They have talent, but not experience. My best years coaching, I was in our base defense about 75% of the time. We’ve got to tackle better — if you can’t tackle, it doesn’t really matter. We’re going a little more old school there. That’s the way I was taught, and that’s what we’re going to do.” # – Region Game For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WDHN - wdhn.com.
